content.text:
I fixed the bug: `[visit](http://[2001:db8::1]/)` now renders as `<a href="http://[2001:db8::1]/">`. Both test suites pass: 303/303 in `test/markdown-it` (including the new cases) and 652/652 in `test/cmspec`. I couldn't run the lint or TypeScript type-check because those commands were denied.

**Cause:** `normalizeLink` in `src/markdownit.ts` rebuilds the URL with `mdurl.format()`, which correctly puts brackets back around an IPv6 hostname. It then runs `mdurl.encode()` on the whole string, and `[`/`]` aren't on that function's list of characters to leave alone, so the host brackets became `%5B`/`%5D`.

**Fix** (`src/markdownit.ts`): when the hostname contains a `:` (meaning it's an IPv6 literal), the URL is encoded in three pieces:
- the part before the host (scheme and `user@`), encoded as before;
- the host itself, encoded, with the brackets added back around it unencoded;
- the rest (port, path, query, fragment), encoded as before.

Brackets anywhere else in a URL are still percent-encoded, so `http://[::1]/a[b]` → `http://[::1]/a%5Bb%5D`. All other URLs go through the original code path unchanged.

**Tests:** I added three cases to `test/fixtures/markdown-it/normalize.txt`: the reported example, one with user info, port and brackets in the path, query and fragment, and an autolink `<http://[::1]/>`.

To finish the check, run `npm run lint` and `npm run type-check`. The new code uses an object spread on the parsed URL. I found no local type definitions for `mdurl` in `src/`, so I don't expect a type error there.
